message.reasoning:
We need to create a JUnit 4 test file DataUtilTest.java covering all methods in DataUtil. Need to include start and end markers. We'll need to test:

- crossStreams: ensure bytes copied correctly.
- readToByteBuffer (public) with maxSize constraints and with unlimited.
- readFileToByteBuffer: need a temporary file with known content.
- emptyByteBuffer: returns capacity 0.
- getCharsetFromContentType: various cases including null, missing charset, quoted charset, unsupported charset, uppercase, etc.
- validateCharset is private but indirectly via getCharsetFromContentType. Could also test via reflection if needed, but not required.
- mimeBoundary: length and characters from allowed set.
- detectCharsetFromBom via private method; could test via reflection or rely on parseInputStream behavior. But we can test indirectly by feeding InputStream with BOM bytes and verifying charset detection leads to proper parsing. parseInputStream is package-private static (default) and we can call via reflection? It's package-private, same package org.jsoup.helper, test class can be in same package to access default methods. We'll place test class in same package org.jsoup.helper to access package-private methods. Then we can call detectCharsetFromBom via reflection (private). But we can test parseInputStream with BOM.

- parseInputStream: test with null InputStream returns Document with baseUri set and empty body; test with InputStream containing HTML with meta charset detection; test with provided charset; test with BOM detection; test with XML declaration; test with unsupported charset fallback.

We also need to test that Validate.notEmpty throws exception when charsetName empty? That's internal. parseInputStream when charsetName non-null but empty string will cause Validate.notEmpty to throw IllegalArgumentException (or IllegalArgumentException?). Validate is from org.jsoup.helper.Validate likely; we can test that.

But we may not have access to Validate class; it's part of jsoup. We'll just test that passing empty string leads to IllegalArgumentException.

Also test mimeBoundary characters allowed.

Implementation details:

We'll create temporary files using java.io.File.createTempFile and deleteOnExit.

For crossStreams test: create ByteArrayInputStream with known bytes, ByteArrayOutputStream, call DataUtil.crossStreams via reflection (method is package-private static). Since same package, we can call directly. It is default access, static, so accessible.

For readToByteBuffer: create InputStream with known bytes, call DataUtil.readToByteBuffer(in, maxSize) and verify buffer limit.

When maxSize smaller than stream length, should read only up to maxSize? Implementation uses ConstrainableInputStream with maxSize limit; we need to verify that returned ByteBuffer limit equals maxSize? ConstrainableInputStream.readToByteBuffer reads up to maxSize. We'll assert that buffer.remaining() == maxSize (or buffer.capacity?). We'll check buffer.limit().

But we might not have ConstrainableInputStream implementation; but we assume it works.

Testing readFileToByteBuffer: write known bytes to file, call method, verify content.

Testing getCharsetFromContentType:

- null => null
- "text/html; charset=EUC-JP" => "EUC-JP"
- with spaces and quotes: "text/html; charset=\"utf-8\"" => "utf-8" (validate returns "utf-8" maybe case? Should return as is after trimming quotes; charset is supported, returns "utf-8".)
- unsupported charset: "text/html; charset=UNSUPPORTED-CHARSET" => null.
- no charset: "text/plain" => null.

Testing mimeBoundary: length 32, only allowed chars.

Testing detectCharsetFromBom via parsing:

- Create InputStream with UTF-8 BOM + HTML content with meta charset different (e.g., iso-8859-1) and ensure final charset used is UTF-8 (from BOM) and content parsed correctly (characters). For simplicity, we can have content with a special character like "é" encoded in UTF-8. Provide BOM bytes then UTF-8 bytes. Use DataUtil.parseInputStream with charsetName null baseUri "http://example.com". Expect Document's output charset is UTF-8, and text contains the character correctly.

- Also test without BOM and without charsetName, with meta tag specifying charset iso-8859-1. Provide bytes encoded in iso-8859-1 (non-UTF8). Use default charset detection: default is UTF-8 for initial parse, then meta triggers re-decode with iso-8859-1. Need to ensure resulting document's charset is iso-8859-1 and text correct.

Potentially tricky with encoding; we can create string with "é" and get bytes in iso-8859-1.

Implementation: create byte[] data = ("<html><head><meta charset=\"ISO-8859-1\"></head><body>é</body></html>").getBytes(Charset.forName("ISO-8859-1")); Then InputStream is ByteArrayInputStream(data). Call parseInputStream(null charsetName) (i.e., charsetName null). Expect doc.body().text() equals "é". Also doc.outputSettings().charset().name() equals "ISO-8859-1". However after parsing, doc.outputSettings().charset(charsetName) sets charset. So we can assert.

Testing when charsetName empty string: call DataUtil.parseInputStream with empty charsetName and expect IllegalArgumentException. Need to pass InputStream non-null, baseUri, parser. Use Parser.htmlParser().

Also test when input null: DataUtil.parseInputStream(null, null, "http://base", Parser.htmlParser()) returns Document with baseUri.

Also test readToByteBuffer with maxSize 0 unlimited: just ensure reads all bytes.

Edge Cases: getCharsetFromContentType with uppercase charset, etc.

Now produce Java test file with imports, use JUnit 4 annotations @Test, @Before, expected exceptions.

We need to reference org.jsoup.parser.Parser, org.jsoup.nodes.Document.

Also need to access package-private methods; test class in same package org.jsoup.helper.

Write class DataUtilTest with multiple test methods.

Make sure to include start and end markers.
